newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares end slightly higher, State Bank leads.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares end slightly higher, State Bank leads.

text.p: Shares, led by State Bank of India, closed slightly firmer on the Bombay exchange on Friday,
The market started weakly, but underlying trends were masked by end of week position squaring.
Bombay's benchmark 30-share index ended 17.17 points, or 0.47 percent, to a provisional 3,823.51, off 3,793.83 low.
"It was a dull market. Trade was mostly speculator-driven," said Ketan Jhaveri, chief dealer at Kotak Securities, the Indian affiliate of Goldman Sachs.
SBI jumped 8.50 rupees from a 306.50 low to end with a net gain of 5.75 at 314.75 and traded over 5.8 million shares.
Traders did not attach any particular reason behind the rise and said hectic buying by some operators pushed up SBI.
"The rally in this market-favourite stock helped perk up sentiment," said an equities dealer at a foreign brokerage.
Foreign funds were bidders in blue chips, but trading volumes were low, traders said.
"Buying interest was centred around select blue chips including IPCL, Mahindra & Mahindra, BSES and ONGC," Kotak's Jhaveri said.
U.S. investment bank Merrill Lynch said on Friday it was moving funds into Indian stock markets from Latin America.
Merrill said the performance of Indian equities during the next six to nine months could surprise investors, in a strategy report titled "As We See It: India on Full Throttle".
"We are moving funds into the market at the expense of Latin America," Merrill said.
"Regionally, we think Korea and Thailand will be important stories going out a year, but there may be a near-term opportunity cost of not exploiting the Indian story."
But, Paribas Capital Markets urged investors to be cautious on Indian stocks if Bombay's index touched 3900-4000 points.
Market focus was now on a crucial Sunday meeting of former finance minister P. Chidambaram's Tamil Maanila Congress (TMC).
The TMC's executive committee will meet on Sunday to discuss whether to rejoin the government which it pulled out of a week ago after United Front alliance chose I.K. Gujral as its leader.
